candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care → Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement), printed p.22 / PDF p.26
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement)
candidate.educational_objective: Evaluate a quality-improvement intervention by comparing relevant client-care outcomes after implementation with appropriate baseline data.

options.A: Compare relevant client outcomes before and after the intervention
options.B: Assume the intervention is effective because staff completed the required education
options.C: Continue the intervention indefinitely without reviewing outcome data
options.D: Evaluate only whether the intervention increased the amount of documentation completed

candidate.rationale: The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan places performance improvement within Management of Care and specifically includes evaluating the impact of performance-improvement measures on client care and resource use. Comparing relevant outcomes before and after an intervention directly evaluates its effect on care. Staff education completion, continued implementation without outcome review, or documentation volume alone does not establish that client outcomes improved.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Entry-level RNs participate in quality-improvement processes and evaluate the impact of performance-improvement measures on client care and resource use.
candidate.source_locator: Detailed Test Plan, Management of Care → Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement), printed p.22 / PDF p.26: participate in performance improvement projects and quality improvement processes; evaluate the impact of performance improvement measures on client care and resource use
candidate.source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
candidate.stem: A unit implements a new fall-prevention intervention as part of a quality-improvement project. Which action best evaluates whether the intervention improved care?
